correctness.rationale: Rows and columns of each binary matrix have exactly three ones. Matrix complement proves zero coefficients at odd frequency weight. Row/column frequency toggles span an 11-dimensional gauge, leaving a unique 25-bit frequency representative. Both standalone row-first C++ and independent column-first Python complete integer enumerators produce exactly 297200 admissible tables, transform all 33554432 reduced frequency indices, verify every even multiplier is 16 modulo 32, verify all odd multipliers are zero, min positive absolute value 16 (attained at reduced index 36045), and exact Parseval total 9972377190400. Fourier diagonalization then yields rank=kernel dimension=\(2^{35}\), sharp pseudoinverse norm 1/16, positive condition 18575, and a translation-average range projector of exact ell-p norm one.

value.rationale: The fixed-margin \(6\times6\) 3-regular bipartite ensemble is canonical in binary contingency-table statistics and graph configuration models. Its 297200 members form a natural high-dimensional binary incidence set. Unlike at the \(4\times4\) balanced order, complement symmetry alone is insufficient to forbid even-frequency cancellation because the count is divisible by 32. The uniform exact 16 mod32 theorem resolves this natural first difficult-sized recovery question; it determines the entire Fourier kernel, the exact recoverable translation-even signal space, a sharp 1/16 inverse stability constant, and a norm-one projection, all directly useful in fixed-margin deconvolution benchmarks. This is a motivated complete finite classification, not a claim of an arbitrary-size theorem.
